source_text: Credimus etiam illum tertio die resurrexisse a mortuis, primogenitum consecuturis fratribus, quos in adoptionem filiorum dei uocauit, quos conparticipes et coheredes suos esse dignatus est.
thought_title: The risen Christ as firstborn among adopted brothers
orientation: Augustine is expounding the creed's article on the resurrection, after having treated Christ's crucifixion and burial.
pass_a_gloss: We believe also [that] he on the third day rose from [the] dead, [the] firstborn for [the] brothers [who are] about to follow, whom into adoption of sons of God he called, whom co-sharers and co-heirs his own to be he deemed worthy.

choices.why: Glossary term for Christ as firstborn among many adopted brothers; keeps the familial and resurrection context.

choices.english: for the brothers who were to follow
choices.why: Future active participle conveys that the brothers will follow Christ in resurrection; 'follow' keeps the temporal sequence.

choices.english: into the adoption of sons of God
choices.why: Literal rendering of the phrase; 'sons' preserves the biblical language of adoption.

choices.english: to be sharers and co-heirs with himself
choices.why: Keeps the compound forms with 'co-' to show joint participation and inheritance with Christ.
Deponent verb with personal subject; renders the act of deeming them worthy.

pass_b_english: We also believe that on the third day he rose from the dead, the firstborn for the brothers who were to follow, whom he called into the adoption of sons of God and whom he deigned to make sharers and co-heirs with himself.

problems.source_quote: quos conparticipes et coheredes suos esse dignatus est
problems.why: 'dignatus est' means 'he deigned/condescended,' not 'considered worthy.' God graciously made them sharers, not judged them worthy.
problems.fix: whom he deigned to make sharers and co-heirs with himself
problems.ruling: dignatus est = deigned/condescended, not 'considered worthy'; reverses agency of grace

edits.old: whom he considered worthy to be sharers and co-heirs with himself
edits.new: whom he deigned to make sharers and co-heirs with himself

fixed: Changed 'considered worthy' to 'deigned to make' because 'dignatus est' means 'he deigned/condescended,' not 'considered worthy.'

last_rejected.quote: for the brothers who were to follow
last_rejected.why: "consecuturis" means "those who would follow/come after," not "who were to follow" as purpose; "primogenitus" is title, "firstborn for" misrepresents dative of advantage/benefit as purpose.
last_rejected.fix: the firstborn among the brothers who would follow him
last_rejected.ruling: 'consecuturis' is future participle dative: 'who were to follow' is accurate. 'firstborn for' reasonably renders dative of advantage; no meaning lost.
